history.idea: Calculate the average token count of the target_sample. For each document in the pool, calculate its token count using tiktoken and its 'quality' based on the ratio of unique tokens to total tokens. Filter out documents with very low unique-to-total ratios (potential repetition/junk) and then sort the pool by a score that favors documents with token counts closest to the target_sample average, before returning a shuffled selection of the top indices.
history.outcome: dev 2.5342 against 1.9410 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Calculate the token counts for the target_sample and the documents. Identify the vocabulary (set of tokens) of the target_sample. Score each document in the pool based on the proportion of its unique tokens that exist in the target_sample's vocabulary, then select the top 25% of documents by this score, ensuring at least some variety by using a weighted random selection.
history.outcome: dev 1.9620 against 1.9410 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Use tiktoken to tokenize all documents and the target_sample. Calculate a score for each document in the pool based on the Jaccard similarity between the set of unique tokens in the document and the set of unique tokens in the entire target_sample. Sort the pool by this score descending and return the indices of the top 50% of the pool in a shuffled order.
history.outcome: dev 1.9480 against 1.9410 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Use tiktoken to calculate the Jaccard similarity of token sets between each document in the pool and the entire target_sample, but instead of just taking the top 50% of the pool, calculate a weighted score where the weight is (Jaccard Similarity * log(1 + total_tokens_in_doc)). Rank the entire pool by this score and return the top 25% of indices in a shuffled order.
history.outcome: dev 1.9413 against 1.9410 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Calculate a score for each document in the pool using a weighted hybrid of Jaccard similarity with the target_sample's unique token set (weight 0.7) and the document's 'density' (unique tokens / total tokens) (weight 0.3), and return indices of the top 20% of the pool sorted by this score.
history.outcome: dev 2.5839 against 1.9410 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Use tiktoken to encode the target_sample into a set of unique tokens. For each document in the pool, calculate a score based on the percentage of its tokens that appear in the target_sample's vocabulary (precision). Sort the pool by this precision score descending and return the top 25% of indices in a shuffled order, filtering out any documents with fewer than 100 tokens first.
history.outcome: dev 1.9062 against 1.9410 for the best at the time, KEPT as the new best

history.idea: Improve the selection by prioritizing documents with high precision scores (tokens matching the target sample) and a high diversity score (ratio of unique tokens to total tokens), and use a weighted sort where both factors are balanced. Specifically, calculate score = (precision * 0.8) + (unique_tokens / total_tokens * 0.2), filter out documents with fewer than 150 tokens, and return the top 20% of indices.
history.outcome: dev 1.9091 against 1.9062 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Use a weighted scoring system where the primary metric is the precision of tokens matching the target sample (similar to experiment 10), but introduce a penalty for very high repetition within a document by subtracting a factor based on the document's Self-Jaccard Similarity (size of the intersection of the document's token sets with itself, i.e., the ratio of total tokens to unique tokens). Only include documents with at least 100 tokens.
history.outcome: dev 2.0930 against 1.9062 for the best at the time, rejected
